To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adhesion strength of PVD Cu/low-d k liner can be significantly increased by using SiC:H liner, which has low dielectric constant, and by optimizing the annealing temperature of PVD Cu seed layer.
SiC:H liner/etch stop layers can be used to enhance the adhesiveness and interfacial strength between Cu and dielectric materials.
the SiC:H layer is a promising candidate as the liner/etch barrier in the damascene process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the adhesion strength of electro-chemically plating copper with PVD copper seed layer on SiC:H liner.
the adhesion strength of PVD Cu seed/ECP Cu multilevel interconnections, and the impact of annealing on the adhesion strength and microstructure evolution of Cu seed layer.
the adhesion strength and microstructure evolution of Cu interconnects with different barrier layers, such as Si 3N 4 and SiC:H.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, SiC:H barrier layer can be used in Cu interconnect technology, and it has potential in the future for low dielectric constant ( k <4.2) interlayer dielectrics.

SiC:H is an excellent replacement for Si 3 N _{4} as the liner/etchstop layer in damascence process, and the annealing of Cu seeds at 200  °C in N2 for 30min is beneficial for enhancing the adhesion strength of the Cu layer.
the adhesion strength of SiC:H/Cu interface is much better than that of Si 3 N/Cu interface, especially for the case of the Cu seed layer with the thickness of 500 Å.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adhesion strength of the ECP Cu layer on PVD Cu seed layer is strongly dependent upon the microstructure and the interfacial bonding.
the adhesion strength of the Cu/SiC:H liner interface is higher than that of Cu/Si 3 N 3 interface.
the adhesion strength of the ECP Cu is strongly affected by the microstructure of the seed layer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SiC:H layer with low dielectrics can be an effective replacement for the high dielectric Si 3 N4 liner in Cu damascene interconnects.
the use of SiC:H liner/etch stop is essential in reducing the effective dielectric k of the Cu/dielectric interface.
a thin layer of SiC:H barrier is necessary for replacing conventional SiN 3 barrier layer in enhancing adhesions strength between Cu/dielectrics interconnects.
